checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: ch 24: twenty-six guards and most of the forty self-name at dusk and the crown leaf burns. Usha names herself to the queen. ch 29: Chathu's forty pages prove to be plain ink with no power, and the Thurai, short of captains and denied the shelf, ask for a truce. ch 30: the last four guards and the unbound members self-name (Lata to Usha, Kamalakshi to Janu). ch 31: the queen signs the charter, burns the remaining leaves and gives up the crown's right to any page. Every odiyan is freed, the pass holds, and Varanad keeps a night-guard of bound pairs. Only the ch 32 envoy question is left open.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: All 21 non-series clues pay off on the page. C01, C02 and C04 pay off in ch 16 (living witness rewrites pages; gap in the rule; folded bird is the queen's private hand). C03, C07, C08, C17 and C23 pay off in ch 29 (plain ink; men in grey and coin die laid out as the record; 'Written off. Paid in full. C.'; Rema at the gate). C05 pays off in ch 24 (Usha names herself to the queen). C06 pays off in ch 7 (Ammini's hitch). C09 pays off in ch 25 and ch 28 (strike used once, then lost with the hand). C10 pays off in ch 27 (Asha's words). C11 pays off in ch 26 (Thankam operates). C14 pays off in ch 11 (escort order 'I can write down'). C15 and C19 pay off in ch 31 (groves under Pachan's map; queen signs in full in her own hand, no stamp). C16 pays off in ch 16 (Usha told the queen). C18 pays off in ch 28 (Janu's lamp at the stair). C20 pays off in ch 32 (boat named Kirri). C21 pays off in ch 30 (writ read and handed to Rema). C22 pays off in ch 19 (missed signals explained). C12 and C13 are logged as series threads. No clue is left dangling.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: ch 16: the queen walks into the drying shed and lays down Usha's freshly written page: 'You carried away paper. You can't carry away what I saw.' This recasts the first half's page-burning victory. She owns the folded bird and offers command plus Kettamala for Devan. The romance changes: the offer prices Devan's office against Neela's answer, and Neela sees that 'the only freedom I have ever had is the one that bleeds when he does.' This sets up Devan's unilateral refusal (ch 17), the breach and repair (ch 20), and the shared refusal (ch 21).

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: Opening belief: freedom means belonging to no one (ch 16: 'Freedom was belonging to no one. She had said it to Ammu at fourteen'). The ch 28 choice: she writes her name first on the roll by daylight, 'Indu, called Neela, of Nellimala and Kettamala', and binds herself to the Company's vote: 'If they vote against me, I go with it... For twenty-one years I answered to a number. I wanted to be no one's. I wanted it so much I called it freedom. It was a very quiet cage. Nobody in it ever bled for me.' This is backed by ch 24: 'It is not belonging to no one. It is choosing who you're tied to, and being able to walk away, and staying.' The ch 1 Neela, who chalked her name last to avoid notice, could not have made this choice.

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: ch 27: Vellan dies holding Kamalakshi's carved bird. He stays dead, his body is carried down, and his smear of lamp-black goes on the roll (ch 28). ch 28: Thankam confirms Devan's right hand won't come back and the killing strike is gone ('Then it won't'). It stays lost in ch 32, where he teaches left-handed drills and loses to Muthu. Other permanent deaths include Biju, Sankaran and Chami's cousin.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: ch 1–2: Devan's goal is to hold the Monkey Pass for the hill villages, without office and against the crown's 'as they always have'. In ch 2 the goal 'went hard as set mortar.' He pursues it through ch 5, 8, 11, 14, 23 and 25 for Kesu's people, Parukutty's children and the villages, not for Neela.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: ch 32: a Thurai envoy climbs under a truce cloth to hire the Night Company. With him comes a scarred odiyan whose wrists smell of salt and clove-bark: 'He was in none of it,' a rogue made somewhere outside the Resin House. Neela's unasked question opens book two: 'Who made you? ... And what do they want with free knives?' The book's own question stays closed.

series_threads.thread: Salt-and-clove-bark resin on scarred Thurai wrists (ch 6, ch 8). Ch 32 brings it back in the rogue who is in no ledger. Someone across the sea is making odiyans. Opens book two.

The long, low river shape that no Company scent matches (ch 17, ch 20). In ch 26 it drags Thurai wounded out of the water and doesn't fight. Its maker and purpose are unexplained, and it is not referenced in ch 32. A light touch in book two's opening would keep it from feeling dropped.

summary: Crown of Night meets every book-level promise. The central question (free every odiyan without leaving Varanad unguarded) is answered across ch 24–31: the self-naming dusk, the plain-ink reveal, the last namings and the charter. Only the Thurai hire and the ledgerless rogue stay open as the ch 32 hinge. All 23 outline clues either pay off on the page or are logged as series threads (C12, C13). The ch 16 midpoint recasts the stolen-pages victory and drives the romance through Devan's breach and repair. Neela's belief change shows in action when she writes her own name first and binds herself to the Company's vote in ch 28. Vellan's death and Devan's ruined hand are real, lasting losses. Devan's pass-holding goal stands apart from the heroine throughout. One minor note for revision: the river shape (C13) last appears in ch 26 and gets no echo in the hinge chapter, so a one-line mention in ch 32 would tie it more visibly to the next book.
